title: Slab-built arch bookends in air-dry clay
subtitle: Weighted arch-shaped bookends built from slabs, no kiln required
excerpt: A matching pair of tall arch bookends built from flat slabs of air-dry clay. Each arch is formed by cutting a slab into an arch profile and bending a short wall around it to create a hollow base. Sand or small pebbles fill the base to add weight once the clay is dry.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Slab-building methods referenced from Encyclopedia Britannica 11th edition (1911) pottery entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat sheet of clay rolled to an even thickness, used as the building unit in slab construction
The drying stage where clay holds its shape but is still damp enough to join and refine
Clay diluted with water to a paste consistency, used as an adhesive for joining clay pieces
Fully air-dried and unfired; fragile, ready for surface sealing

content.text: These bookends hold a row of paperbacks without a kiln. Each one is a hollow arch-profiled form: a flat face cut to the arch shape, a short rectangular base wall built from a
slab
strip, and a closed base. Sand fills the hollow base to give the bookend enough mass to hold books upright. The pair takes about two hours to build and dries over three to four days.

materials.name: Clay slip (same clay thinned with water to double cream consistency)
Fine dry sand or small pebbles (for ballast)
Card or paper for arch template

content.text: Preparation
Cut an arch template from card: 12 cm wide, 18 cm tall, with a semicircular arch cut from the top. Both bookends use the same template so they match. Mix a small jar of
slip
and keep it covered. Roll all slabs before joining so they are at the same stage of dryness when assembled.
Rolling and cutting the parts
Roll a slab 8 mm thick using guide sticks. Cut two arch faces from the slab using the card template and fettling knife. Set both faces aside on a flat board.

Cut four wall strips from the remaining slab, each 4 cm wide and 8 mm thick. You need two for each bookend: one strip for the two short sides, one for the back edge. Cut each strip to the correct length once you hold it against the arch face.
Cut two base rectangles, each 12 cm by 8 cm, from a fresh piece of rolled slab 8 mm thick.
Assembling the bookends
Let all the cut pieces firm up to
leather-hard
before joining. This takes about 30 to 45 minutes in a dry room. At leather-hard the pieces hold their shape under the pressure of joining without distorting.
Score the edges of the arch face and the joining edges of the wall strips with a needle tool in a cross-hatched pattern. Brush slip onto all scored surfaces.
Press the wall strips around the edge of the arch face, working from the bottom corners up each side and finishing across the arch top. Hold each join for 30 seconds before moving to the next.

Score and slip the bottom edge of the assembled arch walls and the top surface of the base rectangle. Press the arch assembly onto the base. Reinforce the inside of the joint with a thin coil of soft clay smoothed into the corner on the inside. This is the structural joint that carries the weight of the books.
Leave a 2 cm gap in one side wall before drying. This is the fill hole for the ballast sand. Smooth all outer joins with a damp sponge and wooden rib. The inner surfaces do not need smoothing.
Drying and filling
Allow the assembled bookends to reach
bone-dry

over three to four days. Do not rush drying with a heat source as the thick base is more prone to internal cracking when dried fast. Once fully dry, pour fine sand through the fill hole until the base feels heavy, then seal the hole with a small clay patch and fresh slip. Let this patch dry fully before use.
Finishing

Sand any rough edges lightly with fine-grit sandpaper. Apply two coats of PVA mix to all surfaces. Leave natural, paint with acrylics, or add carved or stamped surface decoration before the first PVA coat. A strip of felt glued to the base prevents scratching shelves.
Variations
Cut the arch face to a pointed Gothic arch profile instead of a semicircle for a different silhouette.
Press a leaf or lace impression into the face slab before cutting the arch shape to add surface decoration.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Walls pull away from the arch face at the joins
items.cause: The clay had dried beyond leather-hard before joining, reducing adhesion
items.fix: Score and re-slip both surfaces. Lay a thin coil of soft clay into the inside corner and smooth it in with a finger to reinforce the joint

items.problem: Base cracks across the middle during drying
items.cause: The base slab was thinner in the middle than at the edges and dried unevenly
items.fix: Press a thin patch of soft clay over the crack with fresh slip, blend flat, and allow to dry slowly under a loose plastic bag

items.problem: Bookend topples forward under the weight of books
items.cause: Insufficient sand ballast in the base, or the base footprint is too narrow
items.fix: Add more sand through the fill hole. For future builds, widen the base footprint to 10 cm front to back
